$comment: App-mirror registry — the ONE list of static hosts that can carry the identical dist (see docs/redundancy.md). deploy/emit-matrix.mjs turns this into the GitHub Actions fan-out. Rules: secrets/vars are NAMES only (values live in GitHub repo secrets/vars, never here); deploy.codeChanges must be "none" for every host (relative base './' + hash routes make the same build run anywhere); max 10 entries. status: live | ready | pending-account | dropped (dropped requires dropReason). Verdicts verified against vendor docs 2026-10-01.

hosts.basePathNote: Served from /drift-shop/ subpath — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Dedicated job in deploy-mirrors.yml using actions/upload-pages-artifact + actions/deploy-pages. Gated on vars.MIRROR_GITHUB_PAGES=true until the owner retires the current branch-based deploy (turn both on at once = two deploys racing).

hosts.headersNote: No real response headers on Pages — CSP rides in a <meta> tag; frame-ancestors/HSTS unavailable (accepted, documented).
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Repo Settings -> Pages -> Source: GitHub Actions (only when enabling the workflow job).
hosts.tosNote: IMPORTANT (verified 2026-10-01, docs.github.com pages limits): GitHub Pages is not intended for or allowed to be used as a free web-hosting service to run an online business, e-commerce site, or SaaS. The current live app door sits on GitHub Pages — the plan is to move the COMMERCIAL app's primary door to Cloudflare Pages / Firebase Hosting and keep GitHub Pages for the manual and docs (its intended use). Do not expand commercial reliance on this door.

hosts.basePathNote: Domain root — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job: wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name=$CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT (cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3; the old pages-action is deprecated).

hosts.headersNote: Can send REAL headers via a public/_headers file later; meta CSP works today. Direct Upload project (not git-connected) so the fan-out ships the exact same dist.
hosts.limitsNote: Free: 500 builds/mo; static requests/bandwidth unlimited; 20,000 files/site; 25 MiB max file. Verified 2026-10-01.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Create Cloudflare account (owner email, no card); Pages -> Create -> Direct Upload project named in CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT; API token with Pages:Edit; add secrets CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN + CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID.
hosts.signupCheck: Email + password signup, confirmation email to click. No phone or card required. Cloudflare sometimes shows a human-check challenge on signup or first sign-in — if one appears, Jesse clicks through it on camera; everything after is API tokens, no further checks.

hosts.basePathNote: Domain root — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job: firebase-tools deploy --only hosting (service-account auth via GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS; firebase login:ci tokens are deprecated upstream). Uses firebase.json in this repo (hosting.public=dist).

hosts.headersNote: Real headers are expressible in firebase.json hosting.headers later; meta CSP works today.
hosts.limitsNote: Spark plan (no card): 10 GB hosting storage, 10 GB/month transfer; over-quota sites are disabled until next month. Never upgrade to Blaze (links a billing account + card). Verified 2026-10-01.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Create Firebase project (Spark plan, no card) under the owner Google account; create a service account with the Firebase Hosting Admin role, download its JSON key into the FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT repo secret; repo var FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID.
hosts.signupCheck: Uses a Google account. Pick an existing Google account under Jesse's control. Firebase itself asks for no card on Spark. Do NOT create a brand-new Google account for this unless needed: Google may ask for phone verification when creating one — Jesse completes that step himself if it appears.

hosts.basePathNote: Domain root — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job: npx surge@0.40 dist $SURGE_DOMAIN (0.40 grammar requires the domain argument — we always pass it).

hosts.headersNote: No custom response headers; meta CSP carries the policy.
hosts.limitsNote: No published bandwidth/storage quota — treat as unquantified fair-use risk, not a hard number. Custom domains + certs free for everyone (0.40 release notes). Verified 2026-10-01.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: surge signup with the owner email (no card); surge token; repo var SURGE_DOMAIN=<name>.surge.sh; secrets SURGE_LOGIN + SURGE_TOKEN.
hosts.signupCheck: Email + password from the command line (surge login). Historically one of the lowest-friction signups — no phone, no card, no known challenge gauntlet.

hosts.basePathNote: Domain root — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job: netlify deploy --prod --dir=dist (netlify-cli via npx). netlify.toml in the repo already declares build + SPA fallback + security headers for git-connected deploys; the fan-out uploads the same dist directly.

hosts.headersNote: Real response headers already declared in netlify.toml (nosniff, frame deny, HSTS).
hosts.limitsNote: CAUTION — new accounts (created on/after 2025-09-04) get 300 credits/mo: a production deploy burns 15 credits, bandwidth 20 credits/GB — roughly ~15 GB bandwidth OR ~20 deploys per month, then the project pauses until next cycle. Tight quota; keep as a backup door, not a primary. Verified 2026-10-01.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Create Netlify account (owner email, no card); create an empty site; add secrets NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN (user token) + NETLIFY_SITE_ID (site API ID).
hosts.signupCheck: Email + password, or sign up with the existing GitHub account (no new password, no phone). Confirmation email to click. If a challenge appears at signup, Jesse passes it once.

hosts.basePathNote: Domain root — relative base './' handles it.

deploy.mechanism: Fan-out job curls the site's deploy-hook URL; Render pulls the same source and builds with the committed render settings (build: npm run build, publish: dist).

hosts.headersNote: Response headers/redirects are configurable in Render's dashboard or a render.yaml later; meta CSP works today.
hosts.limitsNote: CAUTION — Hobby workspace: 5 GB/month outbound bandwidth (cut from 100 GB in Apr 2026), 500 pipeline (build) minutes/mo. Without a card on file, exhausting bandwidth suspends Free services until next month. Secondary door only. Verified 2026-10-01.
hosts.oneTimeSetup: Create Render account (owner email, no card); New Static Site from the GitHub repo; copy the deploy hook URL into secret RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL.
hosts.signupCheck: Email + password, or sign up with the existing GitHub account. No card for the free static tier. If a challenge appears at signup, Jesse passes it once.

deploy.mechanism: Would have been: built on GitLab by .gitlab-ci.yml in this repo when the repo is mirrored there.

hosts.dropReason: Dropped 2026-10-01: GitLab Pages deploys require a GitLab CI pipeline, and GitLab's own docs require identity verification to run CI jobs — risk-scored, possibly a phone number or a credit card ($1 hold) for new accounts. A fresh mirror account cannot be guaranteed card-free, which violates the project's no-card-anywhere rule. (.gitlab-ci.yml stays in the repo for anyone with an already-verified account; it is inert on GitHub.)
hosts.signupCheck: DROPPED — card/phone identity-verification risk for CI (see dropReason). The owner rule (avoid human verification where possible) is a second reason this stays dropped.

deploy.mechanism: vercel deploy --prebuilt (would have been the fan-out mechanism).

hosts.dropReason: Dropped 2026-10-01: Vercel Hobby is restricted to non-commercial personal use only (vercel.com fair-use guidelines, updated 2026-09-14) — 'All commercial usage of the platform requires either a Pro or Enterprise plan.' A sold shop product is commercial use. Pro ($20/user/mo) is the named alternative and is NOT the plan at $0.
hosts.signupCheck: DROPPED — commercial-use terms (see dropReason). Not a verification issue.

deploy.mechanism: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy action (would have been the fan-out mechanism).

hosts.dropReason: Dropped 2026-10-01: creating any Azure free account requires a phone number plus a credit/debit card for identity verification, and the account must move to pay-as-you-go within 30 days or services are disabled. Violates the no-card-anywhere rule before SWA's own terms even matter.
hosts.signupCheck: DROPPED — phone + credit card required (see dropReason); exactly the kind of verification the owner asked to avoid.

deploy.mechanism: denoland/deployctl static deploy (would have been the fan-out mechanism).

hosts.dropReason: Dropped 2026-10-01: since Sep 26 2025, Deno organizations get only unpublished 'restricted' Free limits until they verify by linking a credit card; the usable no-card tier is unquantifiable and materially lower than the advertised 1M requests/mo + 20 GiB egress. Not a safe $0 commercial primary under the no-card rule.
hosts.signupCheck: DROPPED — credit-card verification since Sep 2025 (see dropReason); exactly the kind of verification the owner asked to avoid.
